extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners and patent practitioners (applicants, patent owners, and their attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural standards for filing, processing, and prosecuting ex parte appeals to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB), including notice/brief requirements, fees, pre-appeal review, interviews, remands, and post-decision procedures (including judicial review).

rubrics_metrics.name: Line of demarcation between appealable and petitionable matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The line of demarcation between appealable matters for the Board and petitionable matters for the Director should be carefully observed. Ordinarily, an objection is petitionable, and a rejection is appealable, but when the objection is 'determinative of the rejection' the matter may be addressed by the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of typically petitionable (not appealable) matters include restriction requirements, non-entry of election of species, amendments, and holdings of abandonment. 37 CFR 1.181(f) may dismiss petitions not filed within 2 months; petitions from restriction requirements must be filed no later than appeal; thus petitionable matters will rarely be present by the time a case reaches the Board. Case citations: In re Hengehold; Ex parte Frye.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition and duties of the Patent Trial and Appeal Board
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 6 establishes the PTAB. The Director, Deputy Director, Commissioners for Patents and Trademarks, and administrative patent judges constitute the Board. The Board reviews adverse examiner decisions on appeals and reexaminations, conducts derivation proceedings, and conducts inter partes and post-grant reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each appeal, derivation proceeding, post-grant review, and inter partes review shall be heard by at least three Board members designated by the Director. Only the PTAB may grant rehearings. Administrative patent judges must be persons of competent legal knowledge and scientific ability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may appeal; filing an appeal (notice of appeal)
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal is taken to the Board by filing a notice of appeal. Every applicant, any of whose claims has been twice rejected, may appeal by filing a notice of appeal accompanied by the fee set forth in § 41.20(b)(1) within the time provided under § 1.134.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A notice of appeal may be filed after any claim has been twice rejected, even if the twice rejections occurred across related applications. Notices are reviewed by the Patent Appeal Center. The signature requirements of §§ 1.33 and 11.18(a) do not apply to the notice of appeal. Form PTO/SB/31 or PTO/AIA/31 is recommended. Time limits: normally three months; may be extended up to six months with petition/fee as provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and timeliness for filing a notice of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of appeal must be filed within the period for reply set in the last Office action (normally three months). It may be filed up to six months with an appropriate petition and fee for extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reply (e.g., under 37 CFR 1.111) is filed and later the applicant files a notice of appeal before the Office considers the reply, the notice is defective/premature—the Office will consider the reply first. A notice of appeal filed with an RCE is premature; appeals cannot be filed while the application is under an RCE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption that an appeal is taken from rejection of all claims under rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 41.31(c), an appeal is presumed to be taken from the rejection of all claims under rejection unless cancelled by amendment entered by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appellant does not cancel claims they do not wish to appeal and fails to present arguments for certain claims in the appeal brief, any challenge to those rejections is waived and the Board may affirm rejections against such claims. Waiver can cause jurisdictional consequences in later judicial review (e.g., summary affirmance of nonstatutory double patenting). See Hyatt v. Dudas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature and form considerations for notices of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The rules do not require that the notice of appeal be signed, but other papers or actions included with the notice (e.g., authorizations to charge fees) still require signatures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an unsigned notice contains an unsigned authorization to charge a deposit account, the notice will be unacceptable because the fee is lacking. Use of a separate letter is strongly recommended; Form PTO/SB/31 or PTO/AIA/31 may be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal fees and fee payment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees for appeal actions are set in 35 U.S.C. 41(a)(6) and implemented at 37 CFR 41.20(b): fee for filing notice of appeal, fee for filing an appeal brief, fee for requesting oral hearing, and a forwarding fee to the Board after Examiner's Answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective March 19, 2013, the fee for filing an appeal brief in an application or ex parte reexamination was reduced to $0; a new forwarding fee to the Board after mailing of an examiner's answer was added. Appeal fees due under 37 CFR 41.20 cannot be paid using general authorization to a deposit account under 37 CFR 1.25(b). For reinstatement of appeal, previously paid appeal fees are generally not required to be paid again, except if a final Board decision has been made on the first appeal; if fees increased, pay the difference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docketing procedure when appeal is ready
rubrics_metrics.description: If an appeal is ready for docketing three events will occur: (A) an appeal number is assigned; (B) the Board issues a docketing notice; and (C) the appeal is assigned either to a master docket or directly to a panel of at least three Board members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the appeal cannot be docketed due to matters requiring further attention in the examining corps, the appeal is remanded with an order indicating why and notice mailed to the appellant. The docketing notice or remand order tells the appellant whether jurisdiction is with the Board or the examining corps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdictional transfer to the Board
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Examining Corps retains jurisdiction to consider appeal brief, conduct appeal conference, draft examiner's answer, and decide entry of amendments/evidence filed after final or after notice of appeal; jurisdiction passes to the Board upon filing of a reply brief under 37 CFR 41.41 or expiration of the time to file such a reply (see 37 CFR 41.35).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Patent Appeal Center will forward the application to the Board after jurisdiction has transferred to the Board and after processing any appeal forwarding fee where waiver doesn’t apply. Examiners should not mark appeal documents defective for rule compliance failures since Patent Appeal Center conducts reviews prior to forwarding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of amendments filed with notice of appeal (after-final amendments)
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant files an amendment, a notice of appeal and an appeal brief on the same date after a final action, 37 CFR 1.116 applies; such an amendment is not entered as a matter of right but may be admitted if it cancels claims or complies with form requirements or, for specification/claims amendments, upon showing good and sufficient reasons why not earlier presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments filed after final action may be considered but are not guaranteed entry; if an amendment is filed with a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 and then a notice of appeal is filed prematurely, the Office will consider the reply first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defective notices of appeal and corrective process
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices of appeal are reviewed by the Patent Appeal Center; if defective, the Office will notify the applicant of non-compliance. Notices are defective if not timely filed or if the notice of appeal fee was not timely filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PTOL-461 (Communication Re: Appeal) to indicate defects in a notice of appeal. If an appeal brief is filed without first filing a notice of appeal, the Office treats the brief as both notice and brief; the brief must be accompanied by the applicable fees. If defects are identified after entry, examiner should contact the Patent Appeal Center to determine corrective action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement of appeal when prosecution is reopened
rubrics_metrics.description: When prosecution is reopened after filing a notice of appeal and prior to a written Board decision, appellant must file a new notice of appeal in compliance with 37 CFR 41.31 and a complete new appeal brief in compliance with 37 CFR 41.37 to reinstate the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Previously paid appeal fees generally need not be paid again unless a final Board decision has been made on the first appeal. If appeal fees increased, appellant must pay the difference. A complete new appeal brief must be filed within two months of filing the new notice of appeal (extendible under MPEP § 1205.01). If the first appeal resulted in a written decision, all fees are required again for any later appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Appeal Brief Review Request (Pilot) rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon filing a notice of appeal, appellant may request a Pre-Appeal Brief Review (pilot) by filing Form PTO/AIA/33 and a separate paper entitled 'Pre-Appeal Brief Request for Review' with a succinct set of arguments (not to exceed five total pages, excluding the form). The request must be filed with the notice of appeal and before the appeal brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request applies only to appealable matters (not petitions). No after-final amendment may accompany the request; any such amendment filed same day is considered to accompany the request and makes it noncompliant. Requests not complying must be dismissed and cannot be corrected/resubmitted. Upon receipt, a panel (including at least a supervisor and the examiner) reviews and may (A) keep appeal under appeal, (B) reopen prosecution (possibly with proposed amendments), (C) allow the application, or (D) dismiss the request as noncompliant. The panel decision resets filing time for the appeal brief (one month from mailing or the balance of the two-month period, whichever greater). No interviews while pre-appeal decision pending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews after notice of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: One interview after final rejection is normally permitted (the time from mailing of the final rejection through filing of the appeal brief). No interviews will be granted from filing of a pre-appeal review request through issuance of a decision on the request. Except in unusual situations, no interview is permitted after the appeal brief is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the time specified in 37 CFR 41.35(a) the application is no longer under examiner jurisdiction. Requests for interviews on cases under Board jurisdiction require Technology Center Director approval showing extraordinary circumstances justifying remand to the examiner. Interviews after mailing of examiner's answer but before payment of forwarding fee are generally not permitted because they may confuse the record; unusual circumstances (e.g., appellant cancels all appealed claims) may allow one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forwarding an appeal to the Board (forwarding fee)
rubrics_metrics.description: A fee at 37 CFR 41.20(b)(4) is charged to forward an appeal to the Board after mailing of an examiner's answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal will not be forwarded to the Board prior to payment of the forwarding fee (unless waiver applies). Applicants may wish an interview after mailing of examiner’s answer but prior to payment; such interviews are likely to confuse the record and are generally not permitted except in unusual circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Appeal Center review and handling of appeal documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeal documents (notice of appeal, appeal brief, pre-appeal brief request, request for extension) are processed by the Patent Appeal Center, which reviews for rule compliance before forwarding to the examiner. Examiners should not themselves identify these documents as defective for procedural noncompliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a substantial defect is identified after these reviews, the examiner should contact the Patent Appeal Center to determine corrective action. The Patent Appeal Center may return the application to the examiner for corrections to examiner's answer or other outgoing documents when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of filing an appeal brief without prior notice of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: When appellant files an appeal brief without first filing a notice of appeal, the Office treats the appeal brief as a notice of appeal and an appeal brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For this situation, the brief must be filed within the reply period set in the last Office action and must be accompanied by the fees under 37 CFR 41.20(b)(1) and (b)(2). Effective March 19, 2013 the fee for filing an appeal brief is $0, so briefs will not be held defective for failure to pay this fee while it remains $0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official record on appeal — definition of evidence (37 CFR 41.30)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence is defined for purposes of appeal practice: 'Evidence means something (including testimony, documents and tangible objects) that tends to prove or disprove the existence of an alleged fact...' (per 37 CFR 41.30).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MPEP cites the regulatory definition and explains what may be considered 'evidence' on appeal; the full section provides standards for submissions (see MPEP § 1204.04 for details).

rubrics_metrics.name: Remand to examiner when appeal not docketable
rubrics_metrics.description: If the appeal cannot be docketed due to matters requiring further attention in the Patent Examining Corps, the appeal will be remanded to the examining corps with an order indicating why the appeal cannot be docketed. A copy of the order will be mailed to the appellant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The remand order explains why the appeal cannot be docketed; the docketing notice or order informs whether the appeal is under Board jurisdiction or being returned to the examining corps to resolve matters before decision. The appellant will know which organization to expect the next communication from.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals by patent owner in reexamination proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owners may appeal to the Board from adverse decisions in ex parte reexamination proceedings per 37 CFR 41.31(a)(2) and (a)(3), with timing depending on the filing date of the reexamination (before vs on/after Nov 29, 1999).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In ex parte reexamination filed before Nov 29, 1999, a patent owner may appeal after the second rejection. For reexamination filed on/after Nov 29, 1999, a patent owner may appeal only after final rejection of one or more claims for which appeal is sought. Use Form PTO/AIA/31 for filing notice of appeal in reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for judicial review and appeals to the Federal Circuit (35 U.S.C. 142-144)
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing an appeal to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit requires filing in the PTO a written notice of appeal directed to the Director within the prescribed time (not less than 60 days after decision), filing a copy with the Board, and filing a copy plus docket fee with the Federal Circuit clerk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A notice of appeal to the Federal Circuit must actually reach the PTO within the time specified in 37 CFR 90.3 or be mailed by Priority Mail Express per 37 CFR 1.10. The Solicitor may seek remand to the PTO prior to court decision. The Director transmits a certified list of the record to the court and may intervene in certain appeals (35 U.S.C. 143).

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of court papers on the Director / Office of the Solicitor
rubrics_metrics.description: All service copies of papers filed in court proceedings in which the Director is a party must be served on the Office of the Solicitor. Service may be by hand to the Office of the Solicitor (address and hours provided) or by mail to Mail Stop 8 at the PTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 5(b) FRCP and Rule 25(b) FRAP require service on counsel where represented. Court papers sent to other PTO addresses will be deemed served only when actually received by the Office of the Solicitor. The Solicitor's mail service address should not be used for noncourt PTO filings; such noncourt papers mailed there will be returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office procedure following a Federal Circuit decision (mandate and consequences)
rubrics_metrics.description: After the Federal Circuit decides the appeal, the Clerk forwards a certified copy of the court's decision (the 'mandate') which is entered in the application file; the mandate date marks conclusion of the appeal. The Office acts according to whether all claims were rejected, some claims allowed, remand is required, or prosecution should be reopened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all claims remain rejected, proceedings terminate on the mandate date and the application is ordinarily not open to subsequent amendment (applicant must have filed any continuation prior to mandate). If some claims allowed, the examiner should either convert dependent claims to independent form and issue, or set a 2-month time limit for appellant to rewrite dependent claims in independent form. Any Office action proposing to reopen prosecution after a court decision must be forwarded to the Deputy Commissioner for Patent Examination Policy for approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reopening prosecution and remand after court decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a court decision brings up claims not previously considered on the merits (e.g., reversal of generic claims in case of nonelected species), the examiner will take appropriate action; remand and reopening of prosecution may be necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any Office action proposing to reopen prosecution after a court decision must be forwarded for written approval. If prosecution is reopened, the statement of the court's disposition is placed in the electronic file and file returned to examiner for action consistent with 35 U.S.C. 141 appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil suits under 35 U.S.C. 145 and 146 — filing and service requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A civil action under 35 U.S.C. 145 or 146 is commenced by filing a complaint in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia within prescribed time (37 CFR 90.3(a)(3)(i)). Copies of complaint and summons must be served on the Director, the U.S. Attorney for EDVA, and the Attorney General per Rule 4(i) FRCP. The party initiating 35 U.S.C. 146 must file a copy of the complaint with the Board within five days after filing in district court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All expenses of proceedings under 35 U.S.C. 145 shall be paid by the applicant. In an action under 35 U.S.C. 145, the plaintiff may introduce evidence not previously presented to the PTO. Failure to timely file the copy with the Board can lead to further PTO action consistent with final Board decision.
